orders.reason: nodules over elbows and knees, recurrent great toe attacks

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: lumps on elbows and knees

58M here because of hard bumps over both elbows and the fronts of both knees that he first noticed over the past couple of months. A couple of them have leaked a white, gritty material. Not very painful.
On direct questioning: for something like ten years he has had spells of a hot, red, very sore big toe (either side), sometimes so tender a sheet hurts. Each one goes away by itself in a few days, so he never brought it up. Last one was before Christmas. Uncle had gout.
Meds: HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 20, ASA 81. NKDA.

Exam: firm subcutaneous nodules over both olecranon areas and both prepatellar areas, a few with reddened skin over them, one on the R elbow with a little chalky discharge. No warmth or effusion in knees. Feet: no active inflammation of 1st MTPs today.

A/P
Nodules + episodic podagra - picture is gout with tophi until proven otherwise. He is on a thiazide.
- Referred to rheumatology for evaluation and long-term management; they can aspirate/confirm and start therapy.
- Keep the draining spot clean and covered.
- For a flare before then, call; we would treat it.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of visit: 02/28/2023
Re: Rodney Jacobs, DOB 09/09/1964
Referred by: primary care

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Jacobs, a 58-year-old retired postal carrier.

History: He describes roughly a decade of intermittent attacks in the great toes - intense pain with redness and swelling, each settling over several days without any treatment. More recently he has developed firm lumps over the olecranon and prepatellar bursae.
PMH: hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: paternal uncle with gout; father with early coronary disease; mother hypertensive; brother with hyperlipidemia.
Social: retired postal worker, never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks per week.

Examination: Multiple subcutaneous nodules over both elbows and both knees, firm, with erythema of the overlying skin; several are draining chalky white material. No acute synovitis today.

Laboratory: serum uric acid 9.5 mg/dL (reference 3.5-7.2).

Impression: Chronic tophaceous gout.

Recommendations:
1. Allopurinol 100 mg daily, to be increased by our office every few weeks toward a serum urate below 6.
2. Colchicine 0.6 mg daily for flare prophylaxis for the first 6 months.
3. Hydrochlorothiazide raises urate; we would ask that primary care substitute another antihypertensive.
4. We will follow his urate and titrate.

Sincerely,
Outpatient Rheumatology

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here to go over the rheumatology letter. Told he has tophaceous gout, uric acid 9.5. Started allopurinol 100 and colchicine 0.6 daily last week; no stomach upset. Rheum wants him off HCTZ.
New: for about three weeks he has felt a pressure in the middle of his chest on his morning walks, mostly on the hill on his loop. Eases within a few minutes when he stops. Never at rest, not at night. No sweats, nausea or palpitations. Father had heart disease at 52.
Meds: HCTZ 25, atorva 20, ASA 81, allopurinol 100, colchicine 0.6.

O: BP/HR per vitals. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Tophi as before.
ECG in office: NSR, no ST changes.

A/P
1. Exertional chest pressure - typical-sounding exertional symptoms with strong family history and HTN/HLD. Resting ECG normal. Referral to cardiology, asked for a prompt appointment. Reviewed red flags: pain at rest or lasting more than a few minutes, call 911.
2. HTN - stop HCTZ given gout. Start lisinopril 20 mg daily. BMP in 2 wk for K/Cr.
3. Gout - per rheum, allopurinol + colchicine. They will titrate.
4. HLD - atorvastatin 20, continue.

documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY CONSULT
Visit: 04/19/2023
Patient: Rodney Jacobs, 58 M
Reason: exertional chest discomfort, referred by PCP

For about two months Mr. Jacobs has noticed a central, pressure-type discomfort during his daily walks that goes away when he stops. He has had nothing at rest.
History: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, recently diagnosed tophaceous gout.
Medications: lisinopril, atorvastatin, aspirin 81 mg daily, allopurinol, colchicine.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father with coronary disease at 52.
Never smoker.

Exam: BP 138/86, HR 78, RR 16. Regular rhythm; no murmurs, rubs or gallops.
Fasting lipids: total cholesterol 190, LDL 110, HDL 45, triglycerides 150 mg/dL.
ECG: no acute ST changes.

Assessment: stable angina pectoris, to be managed medically.
Plan: add isosorbide dinitrate 20 mg twice daily. Continue aspirin and statin. Return in about 6 weeks.

Outside Cardiology

documents.title: Outside prescription fill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fill history: isosorbide dinitrate 20 mg #60, prescriber cardiology. First fill.

documents.title: Saw the heart doctor yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi Doc, just so you know I went back to cardiology yesterday. I finally started the new heart pill (isosorbide) a week ago. My walks are better, the chest pressure on the hill is mostly gone. But I get dizzy if I jump up out of the chair too fast. They said my pressure was 102 over 70 and pulse 94 in the office. They said to get up slow and keep taking it. Should I be worried about the low pressure with my lisinopril? Rodney

documents.title: Re: Saw the heart doctor yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. The nitrate pill commonly does that in the first weeks. Keep taking it as cardiology said, stand up in stages, and drink enough fluids. If you get close to fainting or actually pass out, call us right away. Let's have you come in in two weeks so we can check your pressure sitting and standing.

F/u dizziness on standing after isosorbide started.
Much better. Still gets a brief head rush if he stands fast first thing in the morning, otherwise fine. No syncope, no falls. Walking his usual route with only occasional mild pressure on the steepest part.
Meds: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, ASA 81, isosorbide dinitrate 20 BID, allopurinol 300 (just went up), colchicine 0.6.
Exam: seated BP per vitals; standing after 2 min without symptoms. Heart regular. Lungs clear.
A/P: Orthostatic symptoms from nitrate, resolving. No changes. Uric acid due in a couple of months on the new allopurinol dose; rheum may order, we'll draw at next visit if not.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Gout/HTN f/u. On allopurinol 300 since June. No toe attacks at all since starting treatment. Says the elbow lumps are flatter; no more drainage. Colchicine prescription runs out end of the month, which is the 6 months rheum wanted. Chest pressure only with the hill, rare. Dizziness gone.
O: vitals per flowsheet. Elbow and knee tophi noticeably smaller, skin intact. Heart RRR. Lungs clear.
Uric acid today 5.8 (resulted while he was here).
A/P
- Tophaceous gout: at target on allopurinol 300. Stop colchicine as planned. Copy to rheum.
- HTN: good on lisinopril. BMP ok.
- Angina: stable on isosorbide; cardiology f/u this fall.

documents.title: Annual Physical Examination
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 59 M.
Busy year: gout diagnosed and treated, angina under cardiology. Cardiology saw him 10/30, now calling it angina from coronary disease, staying with medicines for now. Still gets pressure partway up the hill, sometimes on cold mornings, settles with a short rest. Has never needed to stop on the flat.
No gout flares since February. Tophi shrinking.
Meds: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, ASA 81, isosorbide dinitrate 20 BID, allopurinol 300. NKDA.
ROS otherwise negative.
Exam: vitals as recorded. Neck no bruits. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Ext no edema, pulses intact. Small residual nodules at elbows, none draining. Skin otherwise unremarkable.
PHQ-2 0.
A/P
- HTN: high in the office today after rushing in; repeat similar, home log mostly 130s. Continue lisinopril, recheck spring.
- CAD with stable angina: per cardiology, continue meds; seek care for rest pain.
- Gout: urate today.
- HLD: lipids today.
- Prevention: flu today, covid updated at pharmacy, colonoscopy due 2027.

documents.body: Your labs are back: kidneys, liver and blood counts normal; uric acid still at goal on allopurinol. LDL is about where it has been. Have a good winter.

CARDIOLOGY FOLLOW-UP - 04/15/2024
Rodney Jacobs, 59
Chest discomfort is back on his morning walks, now felt over the left chest and going up into the jaw, about ten minutes at a time and resolving with rest. Nothing at rest. Same episodes as last spring and fall.
Medications: aspirin 81, atorvastatin, lisinopril, isosorbide dinitrate 20 mg BID, allopurinol.
Allergies: none known.
Vitals: BP 142/88, pulse 78, respirations 16.
Exam: no JVD, lungs clear, no edema; no evidence of heart failure. Regular rhythm.
Fasting lipid panel: TC 190, HDL 40, LDL 120, TG 150.
ECG: no acute changes.
Plan: given his symptoms and risk factors, proceed to noninvasive stress testing to look for obstructive coronary disease. Continue current medications pending results.

Had the treadmill stress test 5/8; per him cardiology told him it showed the heart muscle was short of blood flow when he exercised (ST changes) and they want to keep treating with medicines. We do not have the report. Symptoms unchanged: jaw/chest pressure on the hill, gone with rest.
Meds: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, ASA 81, ISDN 20 BID, allopurinol 300.
O: BP per vitals, better than at cardiology. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P
- HTN: office BP acceptable today, home readings 130s. Continue lisinopril.
- CAD/stable angina: positive stress test per patient, medical management per cardiology. Requested the stress test report.
- Gout: quiet.

ED f/u. ED record reviewed: chest pressure walking the dog 10/25, came back in the ED, ECG without acute changes, troponins negative x2, sent home.
Since then no further episodes; he has been walking flatter routes. Cardiology appointment is set for later this month.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM - 60 M
Saw cardiology after the ED trip; per pt no changes, keep the pills. Episodes of pressure still now and then on hills, a few minutes, rest relieves. No gout attacks in nearly two years.
Meds: lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 20 qhs, aspirin 81, isosorbide dinitrate 20 BID, allopurinol 300. NKDA.
ROS: neg otherwise. Sleeping fine, mood ok (PHQ-2 1, tired on short days).
Exam: Vitals noted. HEENT nl. Neck no bruit. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Ext no edema. Small firm nodules at elbows unchanged. Skin no concerning lesions.
Plan: labs - CMP, CBC, lipids, urate. Prevention up to date; flu given 11/4, covid at pharmacy; colonoscopy 2027. Return spring.
